subject: Architecture
title: The Louvre: From Fortress to Museum
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Louvre: From Fortress to Museum.

hook.text: The Louvre began as a medieval fortress in 1190 — you can still see its foundations underground.

buildup.text: French kings expanded it for 800 years. Each one added wings in whatever style was fashionable.

discovery.text: It became a public museum during the French Revolution — art seized from royalty, given to the people.

twist.text: I. M. Pei's glass pyramid entrance in 1989 was as controversial as the Eiffel Tower had been.

climax.text: The Louvre houses 380,000 objects. Seeing everything would take 100 days at 30 seconds per piece.

punchline.text: A fortress, a palace, and now the world's biggest museum.

quiz.question: What was the Louvre originally built as?

details.summary: The Louvre began as a medieval fortress in 1190, was transformed into a royal palace, and became one of the world's first public museums in 1793 during the French Revolution. I.M.
details.whyItMatters: The Louvre demonstrates that great buildings evolve across centuries. Its transformation from fortress to palace to museum shows that adaptive reuse — changing a building's purpose — can create something greater than any single original design.
takeaways: Began as a 1190 fortress, became a museum in 1793
I.M. Pei's 1989 glass pyramid now serves as the main entrance
It contains 72,735 square meters of gallery space

faq.question: Why was the glass pyramid controversial?
faq.answer: Critics argued that a modern glass structure clashed with the 800-year-old palace architecture. President Mitterrand championed it despite fierce opposition.

faq.question: How big is the Louvre museum?
faq.answer: The museum covers about 72,735 square meters of gallery space housing over 380,000 objects, of which roughly 35,000 are on display at any time. Walking every gallery would cover about 14 kilometers. It is the world's largest and most visited art museum.
